correctness.rationale: Complementation yields the reflection equation over exact boundaries, and induction identifies all singleton partitions. The only two-Fibonacci decomposition of F_(k-1) gives precisely two offsets of count two (zero excluded when k=5). The 2026 descent identity reduces all windows to these offsets, with explicit handling when H=F_(m-1)-1; every inequality and equality case is proved for all indices. Exact-integer independent dynamic programming checked all 17,683 (m,H) windows for 7<=m<=21, all argmins, plus reflection and singleton cases. Computation does not replace the proof.

originality.rationale: An interval-wise minimum and complete two-offset equality set, simultaneously for every m>=7 and every 1<=H<=F_(m-1)-1, were not located in the inspected sources or previously published results. Chow-Jones 2026 prove short sums and the descent recurrence; Robbins/Weinstein and Chow-Slattery give value-level formulas and singleton/fixed-count information. Their published results do not state the sharp uniform running-window optimization. Priority remains qualified by inaccessible or unindexed older literature.
residual_risks: Historical priority is not fully decidable from searched sources; a less discoverable classical paper may explicitly tabulate these extrema.

General exact formulas for individual R(n), together with known low-count classifications, contain enough arithmetic information to derive this optimization, but no directly covering closed-form theorem was located; scientific distinction is the all-window extremal theorem.
No independent mathematical audit has been performed.
